# Dev Instincts

The reflexes an experienced developer brings that AI-written code and a green test suite keep missing, collected from real misses so they become checks instead of hindsight.

It started from the <private> trial: a procurement app built in a week with Claude Code. The app was refined through independent reviews and fix passes, to learn how deep the process has to go and whether refinement converges.

## Start here
- **[SYNC.md](SYNC.md):** where every file lives, which copy is the source, and the scripts that keep the agents in sync.
- **[WORKFLOW.md](WORKFLOW.md):** how a change goes from request to done: you decide, the devArchitect plans and writes acceptance tests, the coding session builds, the instinct reviewer checks. One writer at a time.
- **[agent/dev-architect.md](agent/dev-architect.md):** the devArchitect, a Claude Code agent (Opus, max effort) that turns a request into a plain-words plan, the decisions only you can make, and acceptance tests with hand-worked expected values. It never writes app code.
- **[agent/instinct-reviewer.md](agent/instinct-reviewer.md):** the instinct reviewer, a Claude Code agent that checks code against everything here, proves what it finds and records it in the ledger. Install: [agent/INSTALL.md](agent/INSTALL.md).
- **[ledger/](ledger/):** the database. Projects are registered in [projects.json](ledger/projects.json) with their kind and who wrote the code. It holds findings from <private> (a web app built with AI), Ferrite (an open-source desktop editor, also 100% AI-written, imported as calibration data) and Django (human-written, mined as reference); the counts are in [STATS.md](ledger/STATS.md). Each is tagged with the instincts that should have caught it. STATS.md ranks the instincts by real cost, overall and per kind of app. That ranking is the reviewer's check order. Only your own projects and AI-written outside projects feed it; human-written repos mined for calibration are ranked separately as reference.
- **[DEV-INSTINCTS.md](DEV-INSTINCTS.md):** 63 instincts (18 approved from the ledger on 2026-10-31). Each has the reflex, the real miss, the question to ask and the test that proves it. A 51-line checklist at the bottom goes into prompts. Numbers are permanent.
- **[knowledge/HUMAN-REFERENCE.md](knowledge/HUMAN-REFERENCE.md):** what 35 outside sources say AI code gets wrong and what human reviewers catch, weighted by evidence: 1 strong, 6 measured, the rest opinion. It gives the reviewer its proportion-and-hygiene pass (scope, size, needless layers, unstated defaults, security basics). Index: [knowledge/README.md](knowledge/README.md).
- **[proposals/](proposals/):** 16 draft instincts still waiting for approval: 5 from Ferrite, 10 from the knowledge base, 1 from Django. Approved drafts stay there with their numbers. `STATS.md` counts the findings each draft has collected so far.
- **[LESSONS-LEARNED.md](LESSONS-LEARNED.md):** what the trial showed, what worked, what didn't, and what to carry forward.
- **[testing/TEST-BATTERY.md](testing/TEST-BATTERY.md):** the fixed yardstick to run every pass.
- **[testing/MINING.md](testing/MINING.md):** how the reviewer's mine mode grows the ledger from mature open-source repos across stacks: what to take, how much, when to stop.
- **[testing/FILING.md](testing/FILING.md):** how to review a live AI-written repo, prove what it finds without running its code, and file the bugs upstream, scored by what maintainers accept.
- **[metrics/CONVERGENCE.md](metrics/CONVERGENCE.md):** the numbers per pass, and the rule for calling convergence.

## Layout

```
agent/
  instinct-reviewer.md    the reviewer agent (copy to ~/.claude/agents/)
  dev-architect.md        the planning agent (copy to ~/.claude/agents/)
  INSTALL.md              install, first run, everyday use
ledger/
  findings.jsonl          every finding, one JSON per line
  projects.json           every project: code, kind, authorship, source, what was mined
  STATS.md                generated: check order, reference rankings, coverage, the reviewer's record
  README.md               the schema and rules
reviews/<project>/         every review's report and its proofs
proposals/                draft instincts awaiting approval (each shows its proposed:<slug> tag)
knowledge/
  HUMAN-REFERENCE.md      synthesis of the outside sources, and the reviewer's proportion pass
  README.md               index of sources with type and evidence strength
  sources/                one note per source (originals stay on the developer's PC)
tools/
---
# The workflow

How a change goes from request to done with four agents and one writer at a time. Before any of it, the agents must be in sync (`SYNC.md`).

## Roles

| Role | Who | Model | Writes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Architect and decision-maker | the developer | — | decisions, approvals |
| devArchitect | `agent/dev-architect.md` | Opus, max effort | the plan file, acceptance tests (never app code) |
| Builder | the main Claude Code session in the project | Opus, high effort | application code; commits |
| senior-coder | `agent/senior-coder.md` | Opus, max effort | one design note per rule change, beside the plan; never code, tests or the ledger |
| instinct-reviewer | `agent/instinct-reviewer.md` | inherits the session's model | nothing in the project; findings in Dev Instincts |
| Search helper (optional) | Claude Code's built-in Explore agent | a smaller model | nothing |

**Why it isn't a manager, a lead and a junior.**
- Writing code isn't the bottleneck; checking it is. More writers means more to check.
- Every handoff down a chain loses detail.
- The main session already coordinates.

The split that pays is by **independence**:
- the tests are written by someone who hasn't seen the code;
- the review is done by someone who didn't write it.

## The sequence
0. **Design note (any change to a rule).** *"Use the senior-coder agent: design note for `<rule or finding>`."* It reads the code and data model and writes where each candidate rule breaks. The architect doesn't offer options until the note exists.
1. **Plan.** In the project's session: *"Use the dev-architect agent. Plan: `<what you want>`."* It writes the plan file and comes back with decisions.
2. **Decide.** Answer each decision in a line. This is where the expensive bugs are prevented: every unanswered question becomes a default the code invents.
3. **Tests.** *"Use the dev-architect agent. Tests. My answers: 1 = `<…>`, 2 = `<…>`."* It records your answers, writes acceptance tests that fail now, and gives the builder a handoff block.
4. **Build.** Paste the handoff block into the main session. The builder makes the acceptance tests pass without changing them, runs the project's gates, and commits.

You are working in Dev Instincts, `<projects>\dev-instincts` (DEV_INSTINCTS_HOME). Today is 2026-11-02. Garrett has decided a set of framework changes and named the dev-architect agent for every task. This pass covers Tasks 1 to 5 of his list (documents only). A second pass will do Tasks 6 to 10 (tooling). Build nothing in any outside repo, run nothing from any clone, post nothing; `gh` is read-only (`gh api --method GET`, `gh issue view`, `gh search` only). Dev Instincts' own tools may be run.

Lock: `mkdir <projects>\dev-instincts\.instinct-lock` first (if it exists, read `owner.txt`, stop and report; never delete another run's lock), write `owner.txt` (mode: framework-amend tasks 1-5, start time). Release it (remove the folder) as your very last step after Task 5's commit. One commit per task, in order, each message ending with `Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <<email>>`. Tree is clean at `b27a63c`. Amend existing files; don't rewrite them. House style: plain words, dated decisions attributed to Garrett, no personal names besides Garrett, no emails or private URLs.

Garrett's instructions for these tasks, verbatim:

> TASK 1. testing/CONTROL.md amendments, each dated in section 17:
>  a. Section 1: add the null beside the hypotheses: the arms don't differ beyond the noise floor.
>  b. Repeats: on the first repo both arms run twice (A's second run under section 5's template, a fresh file-mode session, same sha). The within-arm difference is the noise floor; a between-arm gap smaller than it is reported as no difference.
>  c. The judge runs twice, fresh sessions, same claims.md; the agreement rate is recorded and disagreements go to a third run.
>  d. Section 14 replaced by Garrett's decision of 2026-11-02: three repos is the first checkpoint, reported as descriptive only; the pre-registered test is five repos, read as a sign test on direction (five of five one way is p = 0.03 one-sided) with effect sizes and ranges; no claim of significance before five; no measure added after the data. The architect's "pooled and 2 of 3" reading is struck, with the date.
>  e. Provenance per run: model id, Claude Code version, effort, date and time, sha, prompt hash, tokens, and the session transcript: Garrett runs /export at the end of each arm and judge session, the file is scrubbed with the work folder's export/sanitize.py, and it goes in the round folder. A run without its transcript is unverifiable and void.
>  f. Section 15: every judge-confirmed data-loss, crash or wrong-result finding is filed whatever its arm; any one Garrett holds back is recorded in FILED.md with the reason.
>  g. Section 16: the judge is the same model family as the arms, stated per run; the same agents wrote arm A's method and both prompts. Item 10: the flags --safe-mode, --strict-mcp-config, --effort, --tools, --disallowedTools and --permission-mode auto were checked against claude --help of 2.1.317 on 2026-11-02 by the coordinator; the environment variable is still unverified and is redundant with --safe-mode.
>  Commit.
>
> TASK 2. metrics/CONTROL.md: the monize row gains arm A run 2, arm B runs 1 and 2, judge runs 1 and 2, all pending; the "Repos with verdicts" line says 0 of 5 with 3 as the descriptive checkpoint. Commit.
>
> TASK 3. testing/FILING.md additions: (a) section 1, a sixth check: read CONTRIBUTING, the issue templates and the security policy for any rule on AI-assisted or AI-generated reports, quote it, and skip the repo if it bans them; (b) section 8: every judge-confirmed finding is filed whatever its arm, a held-back one recorded in FILED.md with the reason; (c) section 7: the round folder keeps the scrubbed session transcript as CONTROL.md says. Re-check monize against (a) now, read-only, and record the result in reviews/monize/. Commit.
>
> TASK 4. PRINCIPLES.md at the root, linked from README.md, dated, in Garrett's words. Four sections: (1) the markers: a result counts only when someone else can rerun it and get the same answer: pre-registered measures, a control, blinding, negative results published, prompts and shas frozen so a round can be rerun on a new model; rounds that lost reported like rounds that won; (2) the test for every addition: a rule, check or step is added only if it comes from a logged failure or enables a measure, with its cost written beside it; rigor that doesn't change what the data can say is not added; the record: the 2026-11-01 <private> round had five stop rules and no cost rule; (3) the record and the protocol: the record is append-only, every rule ever written with its origin, rounds and measured effect, never edited or shortened; the protocol in force is versioned, each version dated with the record entries that put a rule in or out; a rule measured at no effect leaves the protocol and stays in the record; (4) the road, in order: the pre-registered multi-repo result with a control; one outside replication on a repo Garrett didn't pick; a cadence of one repo a month under the same protocol with a public, dated scoreboard; reruns of frozen rounds against new models. Commit.
>
> TASK 5. RULES.md at the root, append-only: the inventory of every rule now in force anywhere in the repo (MINING.md, FILING.md, CONTROL.md, WORKFLOW.md, SYNC.md, the three agent files, the templates), one entry each: the rule, where it lives, date added, origin (the logged failure or the measure it enables, or "none recorded"), measured effect so far ("not yet measured" where true). Nothing judged or removed; this is the inventory. Commit.

Facts from the coordinator:
- `claude --version` is 2.1.317 on this machine today. The coordinator (the parent session) confirmed the flags in 1g against `claude --help` of 2.1.317 on 2026-11-02. The environment variable in question is `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_CLAUDE_MDS`, which you wrote into section 7 earlier today.
- The work folder is `<projects>\<private>\` (private, never published); its sanitizer is `export\sanitize.py` with `export\scan.py` and `export\sanitize.exceptions`. Read them (read-only) so CONTROL.md 1e names the right invocation; don't change them.
- For Task 3's monize check: the clone is at `<projects>\dev-instincts\.instinct-scratch\file\monize\` (partial, read-only, may lack some files; use `gh api --method GET repos/kenlasko/monize/contents/<path>` or the readme/community-profile endpoint for CONTRIBUTING.md, `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/*`, `SECURITY.md`, `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE*`). Quote any rule on AI-assisted or AI-generated reports verbatim, or state that none exists, with the files checked and the sha. Record it in a short dated file `reviews/monize/2026-11-02-ai-policy-check.md`, and add a line to `reviews/monize/2026-11-02-93f4e68-review.md` pointing to it (append only).
- For Task 4: README.md's "Start here" list is where the PRINCIPLES.md link goes, near the top. Write in Garrett's voice as his decisions of 2026-11-02; don't invent rationale beyond what he gave. For the record line in (2), the 2026-11-01 <private> round is in `metrics/CONVERGENCE.md` and `LESSONS-LEARNED.md`; cite where its five stop rules live.
- For Task 5: read every named source completely (`testing/MINING.md`, `testing/FILING.md`, `testing/CONTROL.md`, `WORKFLOW.md`, `SYNC.md`, `agent/dev-architect.md`, `agent/instinct-reviewer.md`, `agent/senior-coder.md`, `templates/*.md`). Date added: use `git log --follow --diff-filter=A --format=%as -- <file>` for the file and `git log -S'<phrase>' --format=%as` where a rule was added later; where that's not determinable say "by <file's first commit date>". Origin: cite the logged failure (ledger id, RTIRR entry, LESSONS-LEARNED section, CONVERGENCE row) or the measure it enables, else "none recorded". Effect: "not yet measured" unless a dated number exists in metrics/ or the ledger. Number the entries so later appends can reference them. State at the top that the file is append-only and that this is the inventory as of 2026-11-02, nothing judged.
- Section 17 of CONTROL.md is the change log; every amendment gets a dated line there. Keep section numbers stable; add subsections rather than renumbering, so existing references (section 5 template, section 7 commands, section 8 arm B prompt, section 10 judge, sections 13 to 16) still hold. If 1b and 1c need run-level rows or file names (claims.md, judge-1.md, judge-2.md, judge-3.md), define them, and make `tools/control.py`'s expectations consistent in words only; don't edit the tool in this pass. If a tool change is needed for the protocol to work, say so in your report rather than editing it.

Final message: the five commit hashes with their tasks; the monize AI-policy check result in two or three sentences with the files checked; any tool change the protocol now needs; anything you could not verify. Don't paste the documents.
